subtitle: How Mularaja Forged a Kingdom from a Crumbling Empire

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a throne platform in Patan with stormy sky, Mularaja I in dynamic half-profile rising toward a lion-carved seat
panels.action: Mularaja I stands at the base of a carved stone lion throne in Anahilapataka, hand resting on his sword, cloak stirred by a dry Gujarat wind as half-ruined city walls frame the horizon.

dialogue.text: In the age when the mighty Gurjara-Pratiharas cracked and old kings fell silent, Mularaja rose from Sarasvata dust to seize the lion seat of Patan and carve the first Chaulukya realm.

i18n.hi: जब शक्तिशाली गुर्जर-प्रतिहारों की दीवारें टूटीं और बूढ़े राजा चुप हो गए, तब सारस्वत धरती से उठे मूलराजा ने पाटण का सिंहासन छीना और पहला चालुक्य राज्य تراश दिया।

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over western India map rendered as terrain, with fading emblems of great dynasties
panels.action: The land of western India stretches below: deserts, rivers and coasts, with ghostly banners of the Gurjara-Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas drooping over distant cities as cracks open in their domains.

dialogue.text: Around the middle of the tenth century, the great roofs over north and western India split. Gurjara-Pratihara power waned in the north; Rashtrakuta weight loosened in the south and west.

i18n.hi: दसवीं सदी के बीच के आसपास, उत्तर और पश्चिम भारत की बड़ी छतें चिर गईं। उत्तर में गुर्जर-प्रतिहार ढले, दक्षिण–पश्चिम में राष्ट्रकूटों का दबदबा ढीला पड़ा।

panels.shot: medium wide of a frontier town landscape, focusing on a modest fortified settlement amid flat plains
panels.action: A modest fortified town with mud-brick walls and a few stone towers rises beside a dry riverbed, small shrines and markets clustered within, while distant hill ridges mark the horizon of Sarasvata-mandala.

dialogue.text: Between these fading empires lay Sarasvata-mandala, the country around Anahilapataka, later called Patan. Here, lesser chiefs watched the great crowns falter and wondered who would rule next.

i18n.hi: इन ढलते साम्राज्यों के बीच था सारस्वत-मंडल, अनहिलपटाक के आसपास का देश, जो आगे चलकर पाटण कहलाया। यहाँ छोटे सरदार बड़ी मुकुटों को लड़खड़ाते देख रहे थे, सोचते थे अब अगला मालिक कौन?

panels.shot: slow push-in on young Mularaja in training yard, three-quarter view
panels.action: A younger Mularaja I, bareheaded and alert, practices with a spear in a dusty courtyard, an older trainer in the background, while beyond them villagers and retainers watch with quiet curiosity.

dialogue.text: Later Jain and court poets would weave tales of Mularaja’s birth and kin, binding him to old lines. The earliest copper plate, from his descendant Durlabharaja, simply names him as the dynasty’s root.

i18n.hi: जैन आचार्य और दरबारी कवि बाद में मूलराजा की जन्मकथा बुनेंगे, उन्हें पुरानी वंशों से बाँधेंगे। पर उनके वंशज दुर्लभराज की पहली ताम्रपट सिर्फ इतना कहती है—वह इस कुल की जड़ है।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Mularaja’s face, thoughtful, with faint overlay of imagined scenes
panels.action: Mularaja I stands in profile, gaze distant, as faint silhouettes of rival banners and small forts seem to hang behind him like thoughts of opportunities in the unsettled land.

dialogue.text: Hemachandra, writing two centuries later, would call him nephew of a Chavda chief and heir by fate. Historians today keep that as legend, but agree on this: he saw a chance in the confusion.

i18n.hi: दो सौ साल बाद लिखते हेमचंद्र उन्हें चौहाण सरदार का भांजा और किस्मत से बना वारिस कहेंगे। इतिहासकार इसे कथा मानते हैं, पर एक बात मानते हैं—मूलराजा ने अफरातफरी में मौका देख लिया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Anahilapataka’s streets from above, with Chavda presence implied
panels.action: The streets of Anahilapataka bustle under the watch of a Chavda garrison on a low citadel, their standards fluttering as merchants, farmers and monks move through narrow lanes and temple courtyards.

dialogue.text: Anahilapataka itself lay under Chavda chiefs, linked once to Pratihara strength. As that patronage thinned, their hold weakened. A small frontier town held a throne more fragile than it looked.

i18n.hi: अनहिलपटाक खुद चौहाण सरदारों के अधीन था, कभी प्रतिहारों की ताकत से जुड़ा। जैसे ही वह सहारा सूखा, उनका जोर ढीला पड़ा। सरहद का छोटा कस्बा था, जिसका तख्त दिखने से ज्यादा नाज़ुक था।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide of Mularaja rallying a compact warband outside town
panels.action: Mularaja I stands before a compact band of armored horsemen and foot-soldiers on the scrub plain beyond the town, his arm raised as he addresses them with steady resolve.

dialogue.text: Hemachandra sings of twelve battles, of oracles and god’s consent before Mularaja struck. The exact count is symbol, not record. What the pattern reveals is struggle, not a single easy coup.

i18n.hi: हेमचंद्र बारह लड़ाइयों, शकुनों और देव आज्ञा की गाथा गाते हैं, फिर मूलराजा वार करता है। गिनती इतिहास नहीं, निशानी है—यह दिखाती है लंबी जद्दोजहद, कोई एक आसान तख्तापलट नहीं।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of assault on city gate without gore, tension in the air
panels.action: Under a hot sky, Mularaja I leads his men toward the sturdy gate of Anahilapataka, defenders above poised with shields, dust swirling between the advancing lines and the looming walls.

dialogue.text: Some sources say he faced the Chavda ruler in open war, perhaps more than once. Others hint at shifting loyalties and seized moments. The chronicles agree on one point: he took the city by force.

i18n.hi: कहीं लिखा है कि उसने चौहाण नरेश से खुली जंग लड़ी, शायद बार–बार। कहीं इशारा है बदलते साथियों और छीने गए मौके का। पर सभी ग्रंथ एक बात पर मिलते हैं—शहर उसने बल से लिया।

panels.shot: tight mid-shot inside palace hall, contrasting old and new authority
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall, a Chavda throne stands unoccupied as Mularaja I steps over the threshold, armor dusty, sword sheathed, eyes measuring the space that had symbolized Chavda rule.

dialogue.text: Hemachandra blends drama and devotion, telling of a dream of Mahadeva leading Mularaja to victory. Modern historians see instead a military takeover in a time when imperial checks had failed.

i18n.hi: हेमचंद्र कथा और भक्ति मिला देते हैं—कहते हैं महादेव के स्वप्न ने मूलराजा को विजय तक पहुँचाया। आधुनिक इतिहास इसे और तरह पढ़ता है—केन्द्र की ताकत ढीली पड़ते ही हुआ सैन्य कब्जा।

panels.shot: ceremonial low-angle as Mularaja ascends the lion seat
panels.action: In the same hall, now cleared, Mularaja I ascends a lion-carved wooden throne, courtiers and soldiers kneeling around as lamps burn low and a conch-shell rests unused on the floor.

dialogue.text: Here, in the mid-tenth century, he took the lion seat of Patan. Later plates from Durlabharaja would remember him simply as Mularaja, the first Chaulukya, the root from whom their line flowed.

i18n.hi: यहीं, दसवीं सदी के बीच, उसने पाटण का सिंहासन साध लिया। आगे दुर्लभराज की ताम्रपट उसे बस यूँ याद करती है—मूलराजा, पहला चालुक्य, वह मूल, जिससे उनका वंश बहा।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of court assembly, monks and chiefs together
panels.action: Mularaja I sits on the throne while local Brahman scholars, Jain monks and regional chiefs stand in ordered ranks before him, each watching carefully as new authority settles over old networks.

dialogue.text: “If Patan is to endure,” Mularaja says, “its strength must feel just.”

i18n.hi: "अगर पाटण को टिकना है," मूलराजा कहता है, "तो उसकी ताकत को न्याय जैसा लगना होगा।"

panels.shot: wide shot of craftsmen building a temple foundation, with Mularaja overseeing
panels.action: On open ground near the city, artisans lay stone blocks for a new shrine as Mularaja I watches from horseback, priests marking out the plan with cords while villagers bring offerings.

dialogue.text: Tradition credits him with founding temples like the Mulavasatika in Patan, fitting a pattern where rulers anchored new power with stone and ritual. Later ages would repurpose such spaces again.

i18n.hi: परंपरा कहती है कि उसने पाटण में मूलवासटिका जैसे मंदिर बसाए—जैसा होता है जब नए राजा पत्थर और पूजा से अपने राज को जड़ देते हैं। आगे की सदियाँ इन्हीं स्थानों को फिर नए रूप में गढ़ेंगी।

panels.shot: somber mid-wide of the same temple centuries later, subtly altered, with faint hint of later architecture
panels.action: Centuries later, the same site shows altered arches and a changed façade, its earlier temple form partly obscured, as a lone scholar in modern robes studies the layered masonry in silence.

dialogue.text: In the Delhi Sultanate period, the Mulavasatika’s fabric would be reshaped into a mosque. Stones laid under Mularaja’s patronage thus passed through new rulers, new prayers, and new meanings.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली सल्तनत के दिनों में मूलवासटिका की दीवारें मस्जिद में ढल गईं। मूलराजा की छत्रछाया में रखे पत्थर नए शासकों, नई नमाज़ों, नई अर्थों से गुजरते गए।

panels.shot: map-like wide, showing arrows of expansion from Patan toward Saurashtra, Abu and Lata
panels.action: A stylized landscape map centers on Patan, with firm lines radiating toward Saurashtra’s coast, the hills of Abu, and the fertile Lata region, tiny forts and waystations dotted along these paths.

dialogue.text: From his compact base around Sarasvata-mandala, Mularaja pressed outward. Later records and patterns of Chaulukya rule show his realm reaching toward Saurashtra, Abu’s heights and the rich Lata coast.

i18n.hi: सारस्वत-मंडल के छोटे से गढ़ से निकलकर मूलराजा ने बाहरी इलाकों पर दबाव बढ़ाया। बाद के लेख और चालुक्य राज के नक्शे दिखाते हैं कि उसका राज सौराष्ट्र, अबू की चोटी और लाट के समृद्ध तटों तक फैला।

panels.shot: dynamic wide battle tableau without gore, Mularaja facing a distant host
panels.action: On a broad plain, Mularaja I sits mounted at the head of his troops, facing another regional force across an open field, banners snapping, both sides held in tense, disciplined lines.

dialogue.text: Regional chiefs resisted this rise. Jain and Brahman chronicles remember more campaigns, more victories, than we can verify. Yet the copper plate’s very existence proves one thing: his line endured.

i18n.hi: इलाके के सरदारों ने इस उभार को रोका। जैन और ब्राह्मण इतिहास और भी चढ़ाइयाँ, और भी विजय गिनते हैं, जितनी हम साबित नहीं कर सकते। पर खुद यह ताम्रपट एक सच्चाई गवाही देता है—उसका वंश टिका रहा।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Mularaja in later years, studying a copper plate being inscribed
panels.action: An older Mularaja I, beard touched with grey, watches a scribe inscribe a copper plate on a low desk, a priest guiding the text as officials stand ready to carry the grant to its recipients.

dialogue.text: Copper plates in his descendants’ names show how Mularaja’s power hardened into institutions—land grants, alliances, and obligations that outlived battles. His rule became a framework others inherited.

i18n.hi: उसके वंशजों के नाम से मिली ताम्रपट दिखाती हैं कैसे मूलराजा की ताकत नियमों में ढली—जमीन दान, संधियाँ, और जिम्मेदारियाँ जो युद्धों से आगे तक चलीं। उसका राज वह ढाँचा बना, जिसे अगलों ने ओढ़ लिया।

panels.shot: solemn medium shot of Mularaja looking out over Patan at dusk
panels.action: At dusk on the palace terrace, Mularaja I stands with hands resting on the parapet, gazing over the clustered roofs, temples and markets of Patan, the sky above washed in deep orange and violet.

dialogue.text: “A throne is taken in a day,” he muses, “but a kingdom is built in years.”

i18n.hi: "तख्त एक दिन में छीना जाता है," वह सोचता है, "पर राज सालों में बनता है।"

panels.shot: final reflective wide shot of Patan and beyond, fading into later Chaulukya monuments
panels.action: The view pulls back to show Patan and the surrounding countryside dissolving into later Chaulukya-era monuments and towns, hinting at the future grandeur that will root itself in Mularaja’s first gains.

dialogue.text: From a fragile conquest in a broken age, Mularaja forged the first Chaulukya realm. His story reminds us that seizing power is only the opening move; the truer test lies in turning it into lasting order.

i18n.hi: टूटे दौर में की गई नाज़ुक जीत से मूलराजा ने पहला चालुक्य राज गढ़ा। उसकी गाथा याद दिलाती है—सत्ता छीनना बस पहला कदम है, असली कसौटी है उसे टिकाऊ व्यवस्था में बदलना।

subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे मूलराजा ने बिखरते साम्राज्य से राज गढ़ा
